subject.title: feat(memory): default cross-conversation recall for personal installs

question: Should personal-install default-on recall wait for a canonical effective runtime DM-scope input, or is config-only inference an intentionally accepted privacy boundary?
rationale: The answer determines whether dynamic channel isolation is authoritative for private transcript recall; source context identifies a channel path where configuration alone cannot represent the effective isolation scope.

options.title: Carry runtime DM scope into eligibility
options.body: Add a canonical effective-scope input to the recall decision, keep the safer behavior until it is available, and prove isolated senders cannot cross-recall.

options.title: Keep the existing opt-in default
options.body: Leave the merged feature default-off while the runtime scope contract is designed and reviewed.

options.title: Accept config-only inference
options.body: Land the default flip despite dynamic isolation paths, explicitly accepting the resulting privacy-boundary risk.

recommendation.title: Carry runtime DM scope into eligibility
recommendation.body: Add a canonical effective-scope input to the recall decision, keep the safer behavior until it is available, and prove isolated senders cannot cross-recall.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the related private-recall feature and its original privacy boundary through the merged implementation.
